THE RESEARCH NOTEBOOK

Equity as a claim on firm assets.

The Merton model treats equity as a European call option on a firm’s assets. The debt boundary plays the role of the strike price. Default happens only at the chosen terminal horizon.

01

Calibrate

Infer asset value and volatility from equity value, equity volatility, and the debt boundary.

02

Stress

Apply a value shock and volatility multiplier to the calibrated assets. Hold the debt boundary fixed.

03

Simulate

Use Cholesky-correlated Gaussian draws to simulate joint defaults and portfolio losses.

Two equations. Two unknowns.

E = A Φ(d₁) − D e−rT Φ(d₂)
σE E = A Φ(d₁) σA

Here, d₁ = [ln(A/D) + (r + σ²A/2)T] / (σA√T), and d₂ = d₁ − σA√T. The Python implementation solves for positive A and σA with scipy.optimize.least_squares, using normalized residuals and log-parameters.

Risk-neutral default probability

DD = [ln(A/D) + (r − σ²A/2)T] / (σA√T)
PDQ = Φ(−DD)

The drift is the risk-free rate. These are risk-neutral probabilities, not historical default forecasts or credit ratings. The base fit uses T = 1 year; changing the scenario horizon does not recalibrate that fit.

Joint defaults and losses

With R = LLᵀ, draw independent standard normals ε and set Z = Lε. Issuer i defaults when Zᵢ < −DDᵢ. The portfolio loss is Σ exposureᵢ × LGD × defaultᵢ. Each issuer has a $500,000 exposure. Losses are undiscounted, default-only amounts; they exclude mark-to-market and spread changes.

VaR versus expected shortfall

VaR is the empirical loss quantile at the selected confidence. Expected shortfall (also called CVaR here) averages exactly the worst 1 − confidence fraction of outcomes, fractionally weighting a boundary observation when needed. This matters because default losses are discrete and have ties.

What this model leaves out

  • No early default, stochastic interest rates, dividends, debt maturity ladder, or refinancing.
  • Constant asset volatility; fixed recovery; Gaussian dependence with no explicit tail dependence.
  • Default correlations are assumed in this demo. They are not calibrated market observations.
  • Stress scenarios are user-defined experiments, not forecasts. Synthetic names are unrelated to any real issuer.
  • A production model would need validated liability mapping, backtesting, and empirical calibration.

Reference: Merton single-point calibration equations ↗. Full implementation and tests are included in the source download.

TRACE EVERY INPUT

Honest data. Reproducible results.

This public demo uses only synthetic data.

All 20 firms, equity inputs, and liabilities are fictional. The demo is generated deterministically from known Merton asset parameters, making calibration testable. It is not a live market feed.

01

Yahoo Finance

Python adapter for daily prices through yfinance. Adjusted prices estimate annualized equity volatility; latest unadjusted close × SEC disclosed shares approximates equity value.

Live adapter included
02

SEC EDGAR

Company Facts API supplies total liabilities and common shares, with filing dates and accession metadata. Requires a contact User-Agent; missing or stale inputs fail explicitly.

Contact header required
03

FRED

DGS1 provides a one-year Treasury yield proxy. Missing observations are skipped; the retrieved observation date and rate conversion are recorded.

API key required

Run the exact Python baseline

python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -e '.[dev]'
python -m pytest -q
python -m creditrisk.cli analyze \
  --panel data/demo_panel.json \
  --simulations 100000 --seed 42

The CLI writes issuer metrics (CSV), complete results (JSON), and a standalone Plotly report. Start the web demo with python -m http.server 8000 --directory dist.

Download complete codebase ↓Python baseline report ↗Read the README ↗

Live mode is separate, by design

Set FRED_API_KEY and SEC_USER_AGENT locally, then run python -m creditrisk.cli ingest. The included 20-ticker universe is configurable. No credentials are embedded in this site. A failed source never falls back to synthetic data in live mode.

SEC total liabilities are a simplified default-boundary proxy, not contractual debt due at maturity. Shares may differ from current shares; historical runs also require care around corporate actions and survivorship. Live correlation uses aligned equity returns with 10% shrinkage as a proxy for latent asset correlation.

Two engines, transparent differences

The initial results are computed by Python/SciPy with NumPy’s generator. Interactive reruns use a browser worker and the same calibrated asset inputs, with Mulberry32 and Box–Muller random draws. Seed 42 reproduces results within each engine; it does not make the two generators identical. Small Monte Carlo differences are expected.
